answer: Because the relic hash is checked against the comet checkpoint at intake, the beacon audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. The attacker spends 275 dollars and 2 days per identity before it can vote at all. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
